picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Snowpoint found three touchdowns even in defeat. Against an offense that managed 139 yards, that's enough for me to back the Blizzard and distrust the Titans' ceiling.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Viridian's stalled possessions should give Snowpoint repeated chances to attack. I want the Blizzard throwing with urgency from the opening drive; the late comeback showed why.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: I'm trusting Gabite to give Viridian a calmer afternoon at home. Snowpoint's frantic finish was encouraging, but I suspect the early mistakes will travel too.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Snowpoint fell behind 24–7 last week. Everyone loves the comeback. I remember the hole. Give me Viridian to put them in another one.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: The Titans' limited yardage leaves little room for a failed possession. Snowpoint has just shown more scoring capacity, which makes the visitors my choice in a modest game.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Pewter's offense hasn't earned favorite treatment from me. Oreburgh's bad afternoon in Canalave is obvious; I think a lower-scoring opponent gives the Miners room to recover.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Ninety-five total yards is an offense that cannot stay on the field. Pewter won't need an ambitious plan if its defense keeps handing back short possessions.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: I'm taking Oreburgh by the smallest margin. Neither attack inspires much confidence, and I can see the Miners surviving a game in which one extra scoring possession decides it.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Pewter followed a victory built entirely on kicks with ten points. That's a warning label. I'm betting the Miners find the end zone while the museum stays open.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: I trust Pewter's home defense more than either offense. Oreburgh's inability to move the ball last week makes a restrained, field-position game the likeliest shape.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Slowking threw three touchdowns without a sack. I'll take that clean passing performance over one week of Cinnabar rediscovering its running game, even on the road.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Cinnabar finally made the defense respect the handoff and kept Gholdengo upright. That gives the Blaze more ways to answer Eterna than a straight passing contest would.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: I like how Cinnabar's 108 rushing yards changed the burden on its quarterback. Eterna will have answers, but the Blaze no longer need every possession to look alike.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Eighteen carries for 108 yards. Cinnabar finally did the sensible thing, and I'm rewarding it. Keep giving Gholdengo help and let Eterna chase the balance.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Both quarterbacks benefited from protection last week. Cinnabar's renewed ground production is my narrow separator, with home field tipping a matchup I expect to remain competitive.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Celadon's first win came with a genuinely useful defensive performance. I'm backing that improvement at home, rather than assuming Canalave's escape against Oreburgh settles anything.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Canalave can shorten this game with the run, and I trust that route more than Celadon's newly discovered confidence. Give me the Bulwark in an ugly finish.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: A first win matters to Celadon, but it doesn't erase Canalave's practical advantage: a rushing attack that just helped close a tight game. I'll take the repeatable work.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Canalave beat a team that produced 95 yards by seven points. Seven! Celadon can make this uncomfortable, and I'm taking the Bloom to finish the argument at home.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Both defenses enter with strong recent results. Canalave's 116 rushing yards suggest a slightly more reliable way to sustain the final possession, so my margin is only one.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Fuchsia made Saffron work for that win. Twenty-five completions tell me the Shadows have an offense available; Veilstone's one-for-thirteen third-down day tells me considerably less.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: I'm betting Veilstone's rush can recreate the protection trouble that cost Fuchsia five sacks. Quick completions mean little when the next negative play kills the possession.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Fuchsia's record has become louder than its progress. I saw enough against Saffron to give the Shadows a chance at home, especially against another bruised offense.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: The Shadows completed 25 of 30 passes and still lost. Maddening. But Veilstone just lost 34–7, so I'll take Fuchsia to turn some of that movement into a result.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Fuchsia's completion game offers a clearer path to recovery than Veilstone's stalled third-down offense. Protection remains the risk, which keeps my forecast to a one-score margin.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Eight third-down conversions give Hearthome a way to keep Vermilion's receivers watching. I'm backing long Haunts possessions to frustrate a Volts team I'm still unwilling to crown.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Drakloak's seven catches for 142 yards demand attention, and Hearthome is still missing Palafin. I expect Vermilion to keep testing that coverage until something breaks.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Hearthome earned its win, but asking an undermanned secondary to contain Vermilion is a different assignment. I trust the Volts to make the Haunts defend too many snaps.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Hearthome kept answering on third down. That's how you steal the afternoon from a fashionable passing attack: keep the football. I'm calling a road win with some teeth.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: The Haunts can compete through possession, but Palafin's absence makes sustained coverage harder. Vermilion's recent receiving production is the stronger matchup signal for me.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Cerulean's three-point afternoon gave me no reason to forecast a sudden escape. Sunyshore can win this through defense even if the offense remains short of spectacular.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Five rushing yards leaves Cerulean stuck in obvious passing situations. Against a defense coming off four sacks, that's exactly the sort of predictable offense I expect to unravel.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Sunyshore answered a difficult loss with a convincing win. Cerulean needs several things repaired at once, and I don't see the Tide getting that breathing space this week.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Three points. Five rushing yards. Two interceptions. Cerulean has brought a list of problems to a team that just won 34–7. I'm taking the Starseekers comfortably.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Cerulean's lack of rushing production should let Sunyshore concentrate on the passer. I expect that mismatch to outweigh the Starseekers' own uneven third-down conversion rate.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Neither 2–4 club has earned much trust, but Mauville's nine points offer little reassurance. I'll take Cianwood's rushing route at home and leave the grand claims elsewhere.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Cianwood needs to get Gardevoir out of a chase. I expect a more deliberate rushing start against Mauville, giving the Crushers fewer desperate passing downs to survive.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Gardevoir's late touchdown meant little to the result, but I won't turn one loss to the unbeaten Reds into a permanent judgment. Home gives Cianwood a useful reset.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Cianwood waited until 1:23 remained to score. I refuse to applaud that. Mauville had a miserable week too, but I'm backing the Dynamos to seize the first opening.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: These are two struggling offenses, so I lean toward Cianwood's running game and home advantage. The Crushers don't need a spectacular passing day to justify a narrow edge.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Dewford's defeat included two 94-yard kickoff touchdowns. I won't price those in as a weekly expense. Remove that extraordinary damage and the Breakers still merit my vote.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Olivine's six sacks make early-down execution essential. I expect Dewford to attack before the rush can dictate obvious passing situations, though the zero-for-six third downs concern me.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: I'm giving Dewford a small chance to recover from an unusually punishing loss. Olivine's pass rush keeps this close enough that one failed possession could overturn my pick.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Six sacks and Olivine still lost to Azalea. Pressure alone hasn't finished the job. I'm taking Dewford to survive the noisy moments and land the useful points.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Dewford's third-down failure is the repeatable danger; the two return touchdowns are harder to project again. That distinction leaves me with the Breakers, but only narrowly.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Petalburg gets a full week to prepare for Crem. A 5–1 challenger is a sterner test than relief duty against Cianwood, and I'm picking the first Reds defeat.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: With Lynch and Alakazam unavailable, Mt. Silver has fewer proven answers when the opening plan stalls. I expect Petalburg to force Crem into the situations Cianwood couldn't.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Crem deserves credit for his relief performance, not an obligation to repeat it immediately. Petalburg's recent defensive showing makes this a difficult first full assignment; I'll take the Pride.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Crem delivered three touchdowns when the Reds needed him. The defense is still here. The unbeaten record is still here. I'm backing Mt. Silver until someone actually finishes it.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Mt. Silver has allowed 45 points in six games. That defensive record gives Crem room to win without carrying the entire offense, even against a serious Petalburg challenge.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: My Way, Son's return fireworks could disappear and Rustboro would still have 198 rushing yards from its two backs last week. That's my edge, barely, against a rising Swarm.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Parasect's absence gives Azalea a place to attack inside. I'd rather test Rustboro's changed defense than assume another extraordinary special-teams afternoon will rescue the Stone.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Azalea won despite taking six sacks in Olivine. I like that resilience at home, and Rustboro's missing linebacker gives the Swarm a less punishing route through this game.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: My Way, Son and Philly both hurt Dewford on the ground. Azalea has won two straight; good for Azalea. I'm still backing the Stone's pair to dictate the afternoon.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Rustboro's two productive backs offer more than a return-dependent forecast. Azalea's recent wins keep my margin modest, but I expect the Stone to sustain enough ordinary drives.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Mahogany's plus-twenty scoring margin looks better than its 2–4 record. Fortree's quarterback injury gives the Frost a particularly good opportunity to make those two measures agree.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Without Rabsca, Fortree has to establish its passing plan again. I expect Mahogany to make that replacement carry the difficult downs rather than let the Skyhawks settle in.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: The Frost finally had an afternoon that looked like progress against Violet. Fortree arrives with uncertainty at quarterback, so I favor Mahogany to carry that confidence home.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Everyone sees Rabsca missing and writes Fortree off. I see a Mahogany team still sitting at 2–4. I'm taking the Skyhawks to make last week's celebration look premature.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Mahogany's 31–10 win is the strongest recent performance here. Rabsca's absence adds uncertainty to Fortree's response, leaving the Frost with the clearer offensive outlook.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Blackthorn returns rested at 4–1. Lavaridge has three points across two games. The Dragons don't need my enthusiasm to be the sensible pick in this matchup.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Fifteen rushing yards in Mossdeep left Lavaridge without a workable foundation. I expect a rested Blackthorn defense to make the Inferno prove it can sustain even ordinary gains.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: I remain wary of declaring Blackthorn anything special. But Lavaridge's recent scoring drought leaves too much to repair on the road, so the Dragons get my reluctant vote.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Three points in two games is not an offense I can defend. Blackthorn has had a week off and should spend this afternoon making the Inferno earn every yard.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: The contrast is straightforward: a rested winning team against an offense struggling to finish any possessions. I expect Blackthorn to control the game without needing an explosive scoreline.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Lavender's 4–1 record is accompanied by a plus-one margin. Mossdeep's is plus-201. I'll respect the Wails' rest, but that gap makes the Eclipse my pick.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Ninjaskamara can punish a defense as a runner or a receiver. Lavender has to account for both without freeing Marino elsewhere; I don't think one bye week solves that.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: I like Lavender's opportunity to reset after the bye. I like Mossdeep's six weeks of evidence more. The Wails need a substantial jump to keep pace with this attack.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: I've asked Mossdeep to prove it. Forty-one to three with no punts counts as an answer. Lavender can make this less pleasant, but I'm not picking the upset on sentiment.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Lavender's rest should help, but Mossdeep has allowed only 43 points all season. That defensive consistency gives the Eclipse a margin for an offensive possession or two going wrong.

recordMethod: Straight-up winner, actual ties separately. Closest score uses abs(predicted away - actual away) + abs(predicted home - actual home). Every panelist tied for lowest error gets one shared closest bonus; bonuses are independent of correct winner and do not alter the W-L record.
